sampling_model.design: Observational within-regime sampling from one stable equilibrium law.
sampling_model.units: \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are homogeneous iid cells or systems with fixed variable scale.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is required for SCC recovery; for predeclared distinct vertices \(u,v\in V\), a perfect intervention \(\operatorname{do}(Z_u=x)\) is used only for the union effect set for response \(v\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the statistical margin is cross-SCC covariance separation \(\delta>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Distances and effect sets optimize over every graph-specific compact parameter image; no single fitted coefficient root is treated as known.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Conjecture 5.1 states that SCC-discordant equal-outdegree noncomplete simple digraphs admit a parentally closed strict child-count gap.
The half-trek criterion is sufficient for generic identifiability and has a polynomial-time flow implementation.
Distribution equivalence for cyclic Gaussian directed graphs is characterized by support rotations under freely varying diagonal error variances.
Simple cyclic linear Gaussian graph models have the expected parameter dimension and admit score-based structure learning.
Known-block partial homoscedasticity has a necessary-and-sufficient distribution-equivalence characterization for DAGs.
Equal-variance DAG recovery follows from recursive variance ordering and sample-covariance concentration under signal and eigenvalue margins.
Goodness-of-fit inversion yields confidence sets for DAG orderings and unions of ordering-specific causal-effect intervals.
Repeated perturbation, graph screening, and unions of graph-specific intervals yield post-discovery causal-effect coverage in DAGs.
Test inversion addresses undercoverage after equal-variance causal discovery in a bivariate DAG model.

tldr: For labeled noncomplete simple orientations with a common Gaussian structural error variance, the proposal reduces every comparator-parent closed child-count certificate to a Hall deficiency, proves that the certificate creates an explicit precision-Jacobian rank gap, and targets the universal H-star theorem that two-sided local perfect matchings force equal SCC partitions. Conditional on H-star, the published unequal-outdegree separator yields a generic minimum-dimension covariance-model functional for feedback modules. On fixed finite compact families, cross-SCC covariance-image separation and an upper covariance-eigenvalue bound yield uniform covariance minimum-distance recovery; separate stability, edge, and scale restrictions describe the prospective SEM family but do not enter the displayed recovery bound. Split-sample procedures give honest sets of SCC partitions and union sets for equilibrium perfect-intervention effects between distinct vertices.

project_justification.gap: Static Gaussian feedback models lack a complete, polynomially certified separator for the SCC partition when two orientations have equal labeled outdegrees. The closest paper isolates this boundary as Conjecture 5.1 and proves only an acyclic-side special case.
project_justification.niche: SCCs are coarser than the full cyclic graph but retain the scientifically interpretable feedback modules. Comparator-dependent closure is strong enough to make the rank construction valid and structured enough to reduce exactly to matching.
project_justification.fill: The focal theorem is H-star, supported by the closure-to-Hall equality and the incoming-star rank minor. Conditional on proving H-star, it turns algebraic separation into a generic SCC recovery map. On fixed finite compact covariance families, the statistical bound depends on cross-SCC separation and the upper covariance-eigenvalue bound, while split-sample inversion propagates uncertainty to SCC partitions and distinct-vertex equilibrium effects.

related_work: Drton, Hollering, and Wu (2025) introduce the homoscedastic precision-Jacobian program, prove unequal-outdegree and parental-count separators, prove the acyclic-side graph theorem, and state the SCC boundary as Conjecture 5.1; the present kernel is informed by that boundary but uses comparator-dependent closure and does not claim that the final published equations are erroneous. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012) show how path feasibility, integral flow, and determinant structure can make generic SEM identification polynomially checkable; here only the matching and alternating-reachability architecture is adapted because \(\Gamma_i\)-reachability does not ensure no-sided-intersection paths. Ghassami et al. (2020) characterize cyclic Gaussian distribution equivalence when error variances vary freely, whereas the common scale defining the present varieties is load bearing. Am\'{e}ndola et al. (2020) establish expected dimension and score-based learning for simple cyclic Gaussian models. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize known-block partial homoscedasticity for DAGs; their conditional-residual argument fails inside an SCC and therefore does not occupy the present target. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) motivate the covariance-perturbation step but their source-peeling recursion is acyclic. Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) and Strieder et al. (2021) motivate retaining structural candidates before propagating uncertainty to effects; their formal targets are DAG orderings and bivariate DAGs. Sachs et al. (2005) provide a prospective signaling-network consumer, not evidence for the maintained within-regime Gaussian equilibrium approximation.
technical_internal_limitation: In the accessible arXiv-v1 proof of Theorem 4.11, a selected precision coordinate from the comparator skeleton may couple a certificate-side edge row to a parent that is a comparator neighbor but not a certificate-graph neighbor. Same-graph parental closure does not remove this coordinate. The displayed sparse comparator specialization also reverses the incoming-edge coefficient index under the paper's convention. An exact four-node recalculation gives rank five on both sides for the leaked coordinate set but ranks four and five for the corrected comparator-parent set. This diagnostic motivates Theorem 2 and is not a claim about the unaudited final journal equations or a standalone correction contribution.
honest_scope: H-star remains to be proved for arbitrary multiple-tail disagreements; the one-tail and maximum-outdegree-one results are sanity checks, and the replicated seeded test found no counterexample among 100,000 accepted pairs at \(p=6,7,8\) but is not proof. Generic SCC recovery is explicitly conditional on H-star and identifies only the labeled SCC partition outside a proper algebraic set, not every edge, coefficient, or causal effect. The fixed-dimensional uniform probability bound assumes a finite family of compact covariance images, iid Gaussian sampling, a positive cross-SCC covariance-image distance, and an upper covariance-eigenvalue bound; stability, edge strength, and error-scale margins do not enter that bound. Those separate SEM restrictions maintain the prospective equilibrium family and ensure the distinct-vertex effect functional is well posed. Effect sets union over all retained graphs and parameter roots and need not shrink. Reciprocal arcs, hidden confounding, heteroscedastic errors, regime pooling, time dependence, variablewise standardization, and misspecification of the equilibrium Gaussian model are outside scope.

assumptions.condition: For all distinct \(u,v\in V\), at most one of \((u,v)\) and \((v,u)\) belongs to \(E(H)\).
There exist distinct \(u,v\in V\) such that neither \((u,v)\) nor \((v,u)\) belongs to \(E(H)\).

standard.name: Unique-solvability condition for a linear cyclic SEM

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal F\) is a finite nonempty subset of \(\mathfrak G_p\).
\(\Theta_G\) is nonempty and compact for every \(G\in\mathcal F\).
\(\min_{(u,v)\in E(G)}|\lambda_{uv}|\ge b\) for every \((\Lambda_G,\omega)\in\Theta_G\) and \(G\in\mathcal F\).
\(\underline m\le\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_G)\le\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_G)\le\overline M\) for every \(\Sigma_G\in\mathcal M_G\) and \(G\in\mathcal F\).

definitions.name: Noncomplete simple-orientation class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak G_p:=\{H\in\mathcal D(V):[(u,v)\in E(H)\Rightarrow(v,u)\notin E(H)]\text{ for all }u\ne v,\ \text{and }\exists\{u,v\}\text{ absent from the skeleton}\}\).

definitions.name: Comparator-dependency digraph
definitions.construction: \(D_i(K,O)\) has vertex set \(V\setminus\{i\}\) and arc \(j\to h\) exactly when \(j\in\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\), \(h\in\operatorname{pa}_K(j)\), and \(h\in N_O(i)\).

definitions.name: Local Hall graph
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma_i(K,O)=(P_i(K,O),Q_i(K,O),A_i)\), where \((x,y)\in A_i\) exactly when \(y\) is reachable from \(x\) in \(D_i(K,O)\).

definitions.name: Precision-coordinate Jacobian
definitions.construction: \(J_G:=D\psi_G(\Lambda_G,t)^\top\), with rows indexed by the edge coefficients and \(t\), and columns indexed by the upper-triangular entries of \(\Pi_G\).

definitions.name: Minimum-dimension compatible SCC map
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R(\Sigma):=\operatorname{SCC}(G^*(\Sigma))\), where \(G^*(\Sigma)\) is the \(\preceq\)-first element of \(\arg\min\{\dim\mathcal V_G^\Sigma:G\in\mathcal F,\ \Sigma\in\mathcal V_G^\Sigma\}\).

definitions.name: Covariance minimum-distance selector
definitions.construction: \(\widehat G_n\) is the \(\preceq\)-first element of \(\arg\min_{G\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{dist}_F(S_n,\mathcal M_G)\).

definitions.name: Split-sample structural and parameter sets
definitions.construction: \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}:=\{G\in\mathcal F:\operatorname{dist}_F(S_{n_1},\mathcal M_G)\le r_{n_1}(\alpha_1)\}\) and \(C_G:=\{(\Lambda_G,\omega)\in\Theta_G:\|S_{n_2}-\Sigma_G(\Lambda_G,\omega)\|_F\le r_{n_2}(\alpha_2)\}\).

definitions.name: Equilibrium perfect-intervention derivative
definitions.construction: \(\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda_G):=e_v^\top(I-\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top)^{-1}\Lambda_{G,u,-u}^\top\) for \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\ne v\), where \(e_v\) and all matrix coordinates on the right-hand side are indexed by \(V\setminus\{u\}\).

definitions.name: Union equilibrium-effect intervals
definitions.construction: For \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\ne v\), \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}:=\bigcup_{G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}:C_G\ne\varnothing}[\inf_{(\Lambda_G,\omega)\in C_G}\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda_G),\ \sup_{(\Lambda_G,\omega)\in C_G}\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda_G)]\).

definitions.name: Changed-tail dependency-cycle handle
definitions.construction: Choose maximum matchings in the graphs \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) and \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\), expose one supporting \(D_i\)-path for each matched pair, and form the tail-dependency multigraph whose arcs record which changed tails occur on those paths; use SCC contraction of this multigraph as the starting move for H-star.

statements.statement: For every ordered pair \((K,O)\), vertex \(i\), and equal labeled outdegrees, \[\max_{L\in\mathcal L_i(K,O)}\{|\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\cap L|-|\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\cap L|\}=\max_{A\subseteq P_i(K,O)}\{|A|-|\operatorname{nb}_{\Gamma_i(K,O)}(A)|\}=\Delta_i(K,O).\] Hence a positive comparator-parent certificate exists exactly when \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) lacks a perfect matching, and a maximizing \(L\) is recoverable in polynomial time by maximum matching and alternating reachability.
statements.justification: This theorem turns an exponential closed-set search into the exact Hall object needed by the universal kernel.
statements.gap: Drton, Hollering, and Wu enumerate parentally closed sets; Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give a flow paradigm for a different within-graph half-trek problem.
statements.consumer: A failed matching returns the explicit set \(L\) used by the precision-rank certificate in Theorem 2.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix the ordered pair \((K,O)\) and \(i\in V\), and abbreviate
\[
 A_K=\operatorname{ch}_K(i),\qquad
 A_O=\operatorname{ch}_O(i),\qquad
 P=A_K\setminus A_O,\qquad Q=A_O\setminus A_K.
\]
The equal-outdegree assumption gives \(|A_K|=|A_O|\), and cancellation of the common children gives, for every \(L\subseteq V\setminus\{i\}\),
\[
 |A_K\cap L|-|A_O\cap L|=|P\cap L|-|Q\cap L|.
 \tag{1}
\]
By the definition of \(D_i(K,O)\), the comparator-parent condition
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_K(A_K\cap L)\cap N_O(i)\subseteq L
\]
holds if and only if \(L\) contains the head of every \(D_i(K,O)\)-arc whose tail lies in \(L\).  Thus \(\mathcal L_i(K,O)\) is exactly the family of successor-closed vertex sets of \(D_i(K,O)\).

Let \(L\in\mathcal L_i(K,O)\), and put \(X=P\cap L\).  Successor closure implies that every vertex of \(Q\) reachable in \(D_i(K,O)\) from \(X\) lies in \(L\).  The definition of \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{nb}_{\Gamma_i(K,O)}(X)\subseteq Q\cap L.
\]
Together with \((1)\), this yields
\[
 |A_K\cap L|-|A_O\cap L|
 \le |X|-|\operatorname{nb}_{\Gamma_i(K,O)}(X)|.
 \tag{2}
\]
Conversely, for \(X\subseteq P\), let \(\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(X)\) be the set of all vertices reachable from \(X\) in \(D_i(K,O)\), including \(X\).  This set is successor closed, so it belongs to \(\mathcal L_i(K,O)\).  Moreover,
\[
 Q\cap\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(X)
 =\operatorname{nb}_{\Gamma_i(K,O)}(X),
 \qquad
 X\subseteq P\cap\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(X).
\]
Applying \((1)\) to this closure gives
\[
 |A_K\cap\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(X)|
 -|A_O\cap\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(X)|
 \ge |X|-|\operatorname{nb}_{\Gamma_i(K,O)}(X)|.
 \tag{3}
\]
The two opposite inequalities \((2)\) and \((3)\), after maximization, prove the first asserted equality.

It remains to derive the matching formula.  Write \(\Gamma=\Gamma_i(K,O)\), let \(M\) be a maximum matching of size \(\nu=\nu_i(K,O)\), and let \(U\subseteq P\) be the vertices of \(P\) unmatched by \(M\).  For arbitrary \(X\subseteq P\), at most \(|\operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(X)|\) members of \(X\) can be matched, because their matching partners are distinct members of \(\operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(X)\).  Hence
\[
 |X|-|\operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(X)|
 \le |P|-\nu.
 \tag{4}
\]
For the reverse inequality, start at \(U\) and follow alternating paths that use an edge outside \(M\) from \(P\) to \(Q\), and an edge of \(M\) from \(Q\) to \(P\).  Let \(Z_P\) and \(Z_Q\) be the reached vertices in the two parts.  Maximality of \(M\) implies that every member of \(Z_Q\) is matched, since an unmatched member would terminate an augmenting path.  Every neighbor of \(Z_P\) belongs to \(Z_Q\): a nonmatching edge extends the alternating search, while the matching edge incident to a reached vertex of \(P\setminus U\) is the edge by which that vertex was reached.  The reverse inclusion holds by construction, and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(Z_P)=Z_Q.
\]
The matching edges give a bijection from \(Z_Q\) to \(Z_P\setminus U\).  Consequently
\[
 |Z_P|-|\operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(Z_P)|
 =|Z_P|-|Z_Q|=|U|=|P|-\nu.
 \tag{5}
\]
Equations \((4)\) and \((5)\) establish
\[
 \max_{X\subseteq P}\bigl\{|X|-|\operatorname{nb}_\Gamma(X)|\bigr\}
 =|P|-\nu=\Delta_i(K,O),
\]
where the last equality is the definition of the Hall deficiency.

Finally, \(|P|=|Q|\), again by equal outdegrees.  Thus \(\nu=|P|\) exactly when \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) has a perfect matching, and a positive certificate exists exactly when \(\Delta_i(K,O)>0\).  A maximum matching and the alternating search above produce a maximizing \(Z_P\); taking \(L=\operatorname{cl}_{D_i}(Z_P)\) produces a maximizing comparator-parent closed set by \((3)\) and the already proved equality of the optima.  Directed reachability, bipartite maximum matching, alternating reachability, and directed closure all require polynomially many elementary graph operations.  Hence the stated certificate is recoverable in polynomial time. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(L\in\mathcal L_i(K,O)\) and \(|\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\cap L|>|\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\cap L|\), then there is a set \(S\) of \(m+1\) precision coordinates such that \[\operatorname{rank}J_K[S]\le m+1-|\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\cap L|<m+1-|\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\cap L|\le\operatorname{rank}J_O[S].\] The lower bound is certified by a nonzero incoming-star minor at a stable specialization and persists on a Zariski-open exact-support set; consequently \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\).
statements.justification: The Hall witness has statistical content only after it becomes an explicit graph-dependent algebraic rank gap.
statements.gap: The accessible preprint proof of Theorem 4.11 uses same-graph parental closure where comparator adjacency is required and has an incoming-edge index leak; the final journal equations are unaudited.
statements.consumer: The rank gap supplies the population separator required by the generic SCC recovery map.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put
\[
 C=\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\cap L,qquad
 A=\operatorname{pa}_O(i)\cap L,qquad
 B=\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\cap L,qquad
 D=N_O(i)\cap L=A\mathbin{\dot\cup}B.
\]
The disjoint union follows from the simple-orientation assumption.  Equal labeled outdegrees imply \(|E(K)|=|E(O)|=m\).  They also show that \(L\ne V\setminus\{i\}\), because otherwise the strict inequality in the hypothesis would read \(d_K(i)>d_O(i)\).  Choose
\[
 j_0\in V\setminus(L\cup\{i\}).
\]
For an unordered pair \(\{a,b\}\), write \(\Pi_{ab}\) for the corresponding upper-triangular precision coordinate, and define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 S_E&=\{\Pi_{ab}:\{a,b\}\text{ is a skeleton edge of }O\},\\
 S_-&=\{\Pi_{i\ell}:\ell\in L\},\\
 S_+&=\{\Pi_{\ell\ell}:\ell\in D\}\cup\{\Pi_{j_0j_0}\},\\
 S&=(S_E\setminus S_-)\cup S_+.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{1}
\]
Oriented simplicity gives \(|S_E|=m\).  Exactly the \(|D|\) coordinates in \(S_E\) incident to \(i\) and a member of \(L\) are removed, and \(|D|+1\) distinct diagonal coordinates are added.  Hence \(|S|=m+1\).

Expanding the precision parameterization gives
\[
 \Pi_{ab}=t\left(\mathbf 1\{a=b\}-\lambda_{ab}-\lambda_{ba}
 +\sum_{r\in V}\lambda_{ar}\lambda_{br}\right).
 \tag{2}
\]
For an edge \(i\to j\) of \(K\), differentiation of \((2)\) shows that the row of \(J_K\) indexed by \(\lambda_{ij}\) can be nonzero only in
\[
 \Pi_{ii},\qquad \Pi_{ij},\qquad
 \{\Pi_{i\ell}:\ell\in\operatorname{pa}_K(j)\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Now take \(j\in C\).  The coordinate \(\Pi_{ii}\) is not in \(S\), and \(\Pi_{ij}\) is either absent from \(S_E\) or removed by \(S_-\), because \(j\in L\).  If a coordinate \(\Pi_{i\ell}\) in the last family of \((3)\) belongs to \(S_E\), then \(\ell\in N_O(i)\).  Comparator-parent closure gives
\[
 \ell\in\operatorname{pa}_K(C)\cap N_O(i)\subseteq L,
\]
so this coordinate too is removed by \(S_-\).  Thus the \(|C|\) edge rows indexed by \(i\to j\), \(j\in C\), vanish identically on the columns \(S\).  Since \(J_K\) has \(m+1\) parameter rows,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}J_K[S]\le m+1-|C|.
 \tag{4}
\]

We next certify the comparator rank.  In graph \(O\), specialize
\[
 t=1,qquad \lambda_{\ell i}=\epsilon\ \ (\ell\in A),
 \qquad \lambda_{ab}=0\ \ \text{for every other edge }a\to b,
 \tag{5}
\]
where \(\epsilon\ne0\) will be sufficiently small.  From \(J_O[S]\), select the following rows and columns:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{rows}&\text{columns}\\ \hline
 E(O)\setminus\{\text{edges between }i\text{ and }D\}
   &S_E\setminus S_-\\
 \{\ell\to i:\ell\in A\}
   &\{\Pi_{\ell\ell}:\ell\in A\}\\
 \{t\}&\{\Pi_{j_0j_0}\}.
 \end{array}
 \tag{6}
\]
Both lists have length
\[
 (m-|D|)+|A|+1=m+1-|B|.
\]
Order the rows and columns by the three blocks in \((6)\).  Formula \((2)\) shows that the resulting square matrix has the block form
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
 M(\epsilon)&0&0\\
 *&2\epsilon I_{|A|}&0\\
 *&*&1
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad M(0)=-I_{m-|D|}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, an edge row has derivative \(-1\) in its own skeleton coordinate at the zero specialization.  A row in the first block has zero derivative in an \(A\)-diagonal because the only nonzero edge coefficient with tail in \(A\) is the excluded coefficient \(\lambda_{\ell i}\).  The derivative of \(\Pi_{\ell\ell}=t(1+\sum_r\lambda_{\ell r}^2)\) with respect to \(\lambda_{\ell i}\) is \(2\epsilon\).  Finally, \(j_0\notin A\), so the selected edge rows vanish in the \(j_0\)-diagonal column and the \(t\)-row has entry one there.  It follows from \((7)\) that the determinant of this minor is
\[
 \det M(\epsilon)(2\epsilon)^{|A|},
 \tag{8}
\]
where an empty determinant and a zeroth power are interpreted as one.  Continuity and \(M(0)=-I\) make \((8)\) nonzero for every sufficiently small nonzero \(\epsilon\), including the boundary cases \(A=\varnothing\) or \(m=|D|\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}J_O[S]\ge m+1-|B|.
\tag{9}
\]
Combining \((4)\), the assumed inequality \(|C|>|B|\), and \((9)\) gives the complete rank chain
\[
 \operatorname{rank}J_K[S]
 \le m+1-|C|
 <m+1-|B|
 \le\operatorname{rank}J_O[S].
\]

The specialization \((5)\) is an incoming star: its coefficient matrix is \(\Lambda_O=\epsilon\mathbf 1_Ae_i^\top\), and hence
\[
 \|\Lambda_O\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|\epsilon|\sqrt{|A|}.
\]
Choosing \(|\epsilon|\sqrt{|A|}<1\) gives the stated strict stability and in particular \(\det(I_p-\Lambda_O)\ne0\).  The minor determinant in \((8)\) is a nonzero polynomial in the edge coefficients and \(t\).  Its nonvanishing locus is Zariski open.  Intersecting that locus with the Euclidean-open stability region, the condition \(t>0\), and the complements of the finitely many coordinate hyperplanes corresponding to present edges gives a nonempty set: sufficiently small generic perturbations of \((5)\) lie in the intersection.  Thus the lower rank bound persists at stable exact-support parameters.

For completeness, we now pass from the rank gap to variety separation rather than defining the latter by the former.  Over a field of characteristic zero, if \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\) are rational functions, then
\[
 \operatorname{trdeg}\,\mathbb R(f_1,\ldots,f_q)
 =\dim_{\mathbb R(\theta)}\operatorname{span}\{df_1,\ldots,df_q\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
To verify \((10)\), choose a transcendence basis among the \(f_s\).  Its formal differentials are independent; every remaining \(f_s\) is algebraic over that basis, and differentiation of its separable minimal polynomial expresses \(df_s\) in their span.  Separability holds because the characteristic is zero.  Applying \((10)\) to the precision coordinates in \(S\) shows that the coordinate projection of the precision-image closure for \(K\) has dimension at most \(m+1-|C|\), whereas the corresponding projection for \(O\) has dimension at least \(m+1-|B|\).  Hence the two precision-image closures are distinct.

Finally, the structural equation and Gaussian error assumptions give, whenever \(I_p-\Lambda_G\) is invertible,
\[
 \Sigma_G=\omega(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-\top}(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-1},
 \qquad
 \Pi_G=\Sigma_G^{-1}=t(I_p-\Lambda_G)(I_p-\Lambda_G)^\top.
\]
Matrix inversion is a rational involution on the Zariski-open nonsingular locus.  The nonsingular model images are dense in their closures, so equality of \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\) and \(\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\) would imply equality of the corresponding precision-image closures after applying this involution, contradicting the preceding paragraph.  Therefore \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
The asserted all-size compatibility implication is false.  In \(\mathfrak G_7\), let \(K\) have arcs
\[
\begin{split}
&1\to4,1\to5,1\to6,1\to7,\quad
2\to5,2\to7,\quad 3\to4,\quad 4\to2,4\to6,\\
&5\to3,5\to4,\quad
6\to2,6\to3,6\to5,6\to7,\quad
7\to3,7\to4,7\to5,
\end{split}
\]
and let \(O\) have arcs
\[
\begin{split}
&1\to2,1\to3,1\to4,1\to5,\quad
2\to5,2\to7,\quad 3\to4,\quad 4\to2,4\to6,\\
&5\to3,5\to4,\quad
6\to1,6\to2,6\to3,6\to5,\quad
7\to1,7\to4,7\to6.
\end{split}
\]
Then \(d_K=d_O=(4,2,1,2,2,4,3)\), every \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) and \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) has a perfect matching, and hence every corresponding \(\Delta_i\) is zero, but
\[
\operatorname{SCC}(K)=\bigl\{\{1\},\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\bigr\}
\ne
\bigl\{\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\bigr\}=\operatorname{SCC}(O).
\]
Thus two-sided local perfect matchability does not characterize equality of the global strongly connected component partitions.
statements.justification: H-star is the sole global combinatorial bottleneck and the proposal's theorem-level kernel.
statements.gap: Theorem 4.13 of Drton, Hollering, and Wu proves the corresponding existence statement only when one graph is acyclic; no all-feedback proof or counterexample was found.
statements.consumer: Together with Theorems 1 and 2, H-star makes every SCC-discordant equal-outdegree pair generically distinguishable by a computable precision coordinate set.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(K\) and \(O\) be the two displayed graphs in the corrected statement.  We verify every premise defining \(\mathfrak G_7\).  Each displayed list has eighteen arcs, contains no loop, and contains at most one orientation of each unordered pair.  More explicitly, the three pairs absent from the skeleton of \(K\) are
\[
\{1,2\},\quad \{1,3\},\quad \{2,3\},
\]
whereas the three pairs absent from the skeleton of \(O\) are
\[
\{2,3\},\quad \{3,7\},\quad \{5,7\}.
\]
All other unordered pairs occur exactly once in the respective arc list.  Thus the simple-orientation and noncompleteness conditions hold.  Reading the outgoing arcs row by row gives
\[
\bigl(d_K(1),\ldots,d_K(7)\bigr)
=(4,2,1,2,2,4,3)
=\bigl(d_O(1),\ldots,d_O(7)\bigr).
\tag{1}
\]

We next verify the SCC discrepancy.  In both graphs the vertices \(2,3,4,5\) are mutually reachable along the directed cycle
\[
2\to5\to3\to4\to2.
\tag{2}
\]
In both graphs, \(4\to6\to2\), so vertex \(6\) is mutually reachable with the vertices in (2); likewise \(2\to7\to4\), so vertex \(7\) is mutually reachable with them.  Hence \(\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\) is strongly connected in both graphs.  No arc of \(K\) enters vertex \(1\), while \(K\) has arcs from \(1\) into the other component.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{SCC}(K)=\bigl\{\{1\},\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\bigr\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(O\), the arcs \(6\to1\) and \(1\to2\), together with the strong connectivity just established on \(\{2,ldots,7\}\), put vertex \(1\) in that same SCC.  Consequently
\[
\operatorname{SCC}(O)=\bigl\{\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\bigr\}.
\tag{4}
\]

It remains to verify all local perfect matchings.  Only the outgoing rows \(1,6,7\) differ.  Directly from the child lists,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(A,B)&i&P_i(A,B)&Q_i(A,B)\\ \hline
(K,O)&1&\{6,7\}&\{2,3\}\\
(K,O)&6&\{7\}&\{1\}\\
(K,O)&7&\{3,5\}&\{1,6\}\\
(O,K)&1&\{2,3\}&\{6,7\}\\
(O,K)&6&\{1\}&\{7\}\\
(O,K)&7&\{1,6\}&\{3,5\}.
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
For \(i\in\{2,3,4,5\}\), both parts are empty in both orders, and the empty matching is perfect.

For the six nonempty rows in (5), the following paths are paths in the indicated comparator-dependency digraph; grouping their endpoints gives the displayed matching:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(A,B)&i&\text{paths in }D_i(A,B)&\text{matched pairs in }\Gamma_i(A,B)\\ \hline
(K,O)&1&6\to4\to3,\quad 7\to2&(6,3),(7,2)\\
(K,O)&6&7\to1&(7,1)\\
(K,O)&7&3\to6,\quad 5\to1&(3,6),(5,1)\\
(O,K)&1&2\to4\to7,\quad 3\to6&(2,7),(3,6)\\
(O,K)&6&1\to7&(1,7)\\
(O,K)&7&1\to6\to4\to5,\quad 6\to4\to3&(1,5),(6,3).
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
For completeness, we check the arc condition in the definition rather than treating (6) as an unrestricted reachability assertion.  The child and comparator-neighbor sets needed in the first three rows are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
i&\operatorname{ch}_K(i)&N_O(i)\\ \hline
1&\{4,5,6,7\}&\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\\
6&\{2,3,5,7\}&\{1,2,3,4,5,7\}\\
7&\{3,4,5\}&\{1,2,4,6\},
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
and those needed in the last three rows are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
i&\operatorname{ch}_O(i)&N_K(i)\\ \hline
1&\{2,3,4,5\}&\{4,5,6,7\}\\
6&\{1,2,3,5\}&\{1,2,3,4,5,7\}\\
7&\{1,4,6\}&\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}.
\end{array}
\tag{8}
\]
Reversing each path in (6) gives, in its first graph \(A\), respectively,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(A,B),i&\text{reversed path in }A\\ \hline
(K,O),1&3\to4\to6,\quad 2\to7\\
(K,O),6&1\to7\\
(K,O),7&6\to3,\quad 1\to5\\
(O,K),1&7\to4\to2,\quad 6\to3\\
(O,K),6&7\to1\\
(O,K),7&5\to4\to6\to1,\quad 3\to4\to6.
\end{array}
\tag{9}
\]
Every arc in (9) occurs in the defining list of \(A\).  Equations (7)--(9) show for each arc \(x\to y\) displayed in (6) that \(x\in\operatorname{ch}_A(i)\), \(y\in\operatorname{pa}_A(x)\), and \(y\in N_B(i)\).  Hence \(x\to y\) is indeed an arc of \(D_i(A,B)\).  The pairs in the last column of (6) cover both bipartition classes in (5) without repetition, so each is a perfect matching of \(\Gamma_i(A,B)\).  Together with the four empty matchings in each order, this proves perfect matchability for all fourteen local graphs.  By the deficiency definition,
\[
\Delta_i(A,B)=|P_i(A,B)|-\nu_i(A,B)=0
\]
for every vertex and both orders.  Equations (3) and (4) nevertheless give different SCC partitions, which proves the corrected negative statement.

statements.statement: If \(K,O\in\mathfrak G_p\) have different labeled outdegree vectors, then their precision-coordinate Jacobian matroids differ and \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\).
statements.justification: Restating the published unequal-outdegree input makes the two branches of the recovery argument formally explicit.
statements.gap: This is Theorem 4.5 of Drton, Hollering, and Wu and is not claimed as new.
statements.consumer: It closes the comparison branch not covered by equal-outdegree Hall compatibility.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Different labeled outdegree vectors mean that there is an \(i\in V\) for which \(d_K(i)\ne d_O(i)\).  Both graphs are simple and noncomplete by membership in \(\mathfrak G_p\).  The published outdegree-separation lemma therefore gives that \(J_K\) and \(J_O\) represent different precision-coordinate Jacobian matroids.

Let \(\mathcal W_G^\Pi\) denote the Zariski closure of the image of the polynomial precision map \(\psi_G\).  We show that the first conclusion forces \(\mathcal W_K^\Pi\ne\mathcal W_O^\Pi\).  For any coordinate set \(S\), the rank of \(J_G[S]\) over the rational-function field equals the transcendence degree of the precision coordinates indexed by \(S\).  Indeed, after choosing a transcendence basis, its differentials are independent, while differentiation of the separable minimal polynomial of every algebraic remaining coordinate places its differential in their span; characteristic zero supplies separability.  Thus this rank is determined by the polynomial relations, equivalently by the vanishing ideal of \(\mathcal W_G^\Pi\).  Equal precision varieties would have equal vanishing ideals and hence equal Jacobian matroids, contrary to the cited lemma.  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal W_K^\Pi\ne\mathcal W_O^\Pi.
 \tag{1}
\]
On the nonsingular symmetric-matrix locus, inversion \(A\mapsto A^{-1}\) is a rational involution.  By the covariance-variety and precision-map definitions, it takes every nonsingular covariance model point for \(G\) to its precision model point, with \(t=\omega^{-1}>0\), and conversely.  These model points are Zariski dense in the respective closures.  Hence equality \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma=\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\) would, after inversion on their dense nonsingular loci and Zariski closure, imply \(\mathcal W_K^\Pi=\mathcal W_O^\Pi\), contradicting \((1)\).  Thus \(\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_O^\Sigma\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(K\) and \(O\) differ only in edges leaving one vertex \(i\) and both \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) and \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) have perfect matchings, then \(\operatorname{Rch}(K)=\operatorname{Rch}(O)\), and hence \(\operatorname{SCC}(K)=\operatorname{SCC}(O)\).
statements.justification: This reduction verifies that matching-supported path substitution recovers a complete known special case.
statements.gap: The published acyclic theorem uses topological minimality; this statement permits arbitrary feedback away from one changed tail.
statements.consumer: The proof identifies exactly why multiple changed tails, rather than feedback alone, create H-star's obstruction.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(R\) be the directed graph induced by either \(K\) or \(O\) on \(V\setminus\{i\}\).  It is common to the two graphs because every outgoing row other than the row at \(i\) is the same.  Put
\[
 P=\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\setminus\operatorname{ch}_O(i),
 \qquad
 Q=\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\setminus\operatorname{ch}_K(i).
\]
Equal outdegrees give \(|P|=|Q|\).  A perfect matching in \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) assigns to each \(a\in P\) a distinct \(b\in Q\) that is reachable from \(a\) in \(D_i(K,O)\).  If
\[
 a=x_0\to x_1\to\cdots\to x_r=b
\]
is the supporting \(D_i(K,O)\)-path, the definition of every dependency arc gives the reversed \(K\)-edges
\[
 b=x_r\to x_{r-1}\to\cdots\to x_0=a.
 \tag{1}
\]
The dependency graph has vertex set \(V\setminus\{i\}\), so \((1)\) avoids \(i\).  Every edge of \((1)\) consequently has a tail other than \(i\), belongs to \(R\), and is also an edge of \(O\).  Since \(i\to b\) is an edge of \(O\), the \(K\)-only edge \(i\to a\) can be replaced by the \(O\)-path
\[
 i\to b\to x_{r-1}\to\cdots\to a.
 \tag{2}
\]
Common edges leaving \(i\) require no replacement, and every edge whose tail is not \(i\) already lies in \(R\).  Replacing each \(K\)-only edge in an arbitrary finite \(K\)-walk by its finite path \((2)\) therefore produces an \(O\)-walk with the same endpoints.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Rch}(K)\subseteq\operatorname{Rch}(O).
\]
Applying the same argument to the perfect matching in \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) gives the reverse inclusion.  Thus \(\operatorname{Rch}(K)=\operatorname{Rch}(O)\).  Strongly connected components are precisely the equivalence classes of mutual reachability, so \(\operatorname{SCC}(K)=\operatorname{SCC}(O)\).  The closure-matching theorem additionally identifies the two perfect-matching hypotheses with the absence of a positive comparator-parent certificate in either order. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(K\ne O\), \(d_K=d_O\), and \(\max_{v\in V}d_K(v)\le1\), then some \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) or \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) lacks a perfect matching.
statements.justification: The functional-digraph reduction is a nontrivial all-size sanity check for H-star.
statements.gap: It lies inside broader easy graph regimes and is supporting evidence rather than a standalone contribution.
statements.consumer: It rules out the smallest-degree source of counterexamples and calibrates the dependency-cycle handle.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Suppose, toward a contradiction, that every \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) and every \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) has a perfect matching.  Since \(K\ne O\), some outgoing row differs.  Choose such an \(i\).  Equal outdegrees and the bound \(d_K=d_O\le1\) imply that there are distinct vertices \(a,b\) with
\[
 \operatorname{ch}_K(i)=\{a\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{ch}_O(i)=\{b\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the two parts of \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) are \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b\}\).  A perfect matching makes \(b\) reachable from \(a\) in \(D_i(K,O)\).  Only \(a\), the sole \(K\)-child of \(i\), can have an outgoing dependency arc.  Since loops are forbidden and \(a\ne b\), the supporting path must be the single arc \(a\to b\).  The dependency-arc definition then gives the edge
\[
 b\to a\quad\text{in }K.
 \tag{2}
\]
The reverse-order perfect matching analogously gives
\[
 a\to b\quad\text{in }O.
 \tag{3}
\]
At vertex \(a\), equation \((3)\) and equal outdegrees imply that \(a\) has a unique \(K\)-child, say \(c\).  Oriented simplicity applied to \((2)\) gives \(c\ne b\), and looplessness gives \(c\ne a\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{ch}_K(a)=\{c\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{ch}_O(a)=\{b\}.
\]
The assumed perfect matching in \(\Gamma_a(K,O)\), by the same one-emitter argument, forces the edge \(b\to c\) in \(K\).  But \((2)\) and the outdegree-one bound say that the unique \(K\)-child of \(b\) is \(a\).  Therefore \(c=a\), contradicting \(c\ne a\).  At least one of the stated local Hall graphs must consequently lack a perfect matching. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Assume Theorem 3. For every \(G_0\in\mathcal F\), there exists a proper algebraic set \(\mathcal E_{G_0}\subsetneq\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\) such that \[\mathcal R(\Sigma)=\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\qquad\text{for all }\Sigma\in\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\setminus\mathcal E_{G_0}.\]
statements.justification: This theorem converts pairwise algebraic separation into an explicit generic functional for the feedback-module partition.
statements.gap: Drton, Hollering, and Wu prove generic distinguishability for restricted graph families, while Ghassami et al. target quasi-equivalence under arbitrary error variances.
statements.consumer: Within a declared homogeneous regime, the map returns feedback modules rather than forcing a DAG representation.
statements.proof_tex:
The causal structure target is \(\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\), whereas \(\mathcal R\) is the observed-covariance functional defined by minimum-dimensional variety compatibility.  We prove their equality under the finite certificate-separation premise of the corrected statement.

First fix \(G,H\in\mathcal F\) with
\[
\operatorname{SCC}(G)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(H).
\tag{10}
\]
If \(d_G\ne d_H\), the unequal-outdegree separation lemma gives
\[
\mathcal V_G^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_H^\Sigma.
\tag{11}
\]
If \(d_G=d_H\), the certificate-separation premise supplies an ordered choice \((K,O)\in\{(G,H),(H,G)\}\) and \(i\in V\) for which \(\Delta_i(K,O)>0\).  The closure--matching theorem gives a set \(L\in\mathcal L_i(K,O)\) satisfying
\[
|\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\cap L|-|\operatorname{ch}_O(i)\cap L|
=\Delta_i(K,O)>0.
\tag{12}
\]
The incoming-star rank theorem applied to (12) then yields
\[
\mathcal V_K^\Sigma\ne\mathcal V_O^\Sigma,
\]
which is (11) after forgetting the chosen order.  Thus (10) implies (11) for every pair in the candidate family.

We next establish the algebraic facts needed to turn pairwise distinction into a generic selector.  Fix \(G\in\mathcal F\), put \(q_G=|E(G)|\), and let \(A_G=\mathbb A^{q_G+1}\) be the affine parameter space with coordinates given by the allowed edge coefficients and \(\omega\).  Let
\[
U_G:=\{(\Lambda_G,\omega)\in A_G:\det(I_p-\Lambda_G)\ne0\}
\]
and let \(D_G:=U_G\cap\{\omega>0\}\), the domain appearing in the definition of \(\mathcal V_G^\Sigma\).  The set \(D_G\) contains a nonempty Euclidean open neighborhood of \((0,1)\): continuity of the determinant gives such a neighborhood on which \(\det(I_p-\Lambda_G)\ne0\), and positivity gives an open interval about \(1\).  A real polynomial that vanishes on a nonempty Euclidean open set is the zero polynomial, as follows by fixing all but one coordinate and applying the one-variable root bound successively.  Therefore \(D_G\) is Zariski dense in \(A_G\), and hence dense in \(U_G\).

The affine space \(A_G\) is irreducible: two nonempty principal Zariski open sets defined by nonzero polynomials \(f\) and \(g\) intersect because the nonzero polynomial \(fg\) cannot vanish on all of \(\mathbb R^{q_G+1}\).  Every nonempty Zariski open contains a nonempty principal open, so this proves irreducibility.  The nonempty open subset \(U_G\) is therefore irreducible as well.  On \(U_G\), the covariance map
\[
\phi_G(\Lambda_G,\omega)
=\omega(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-\top}(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-1}
\tag{13}
\]
is regular, because every inverse entry is an adjugate entry divided by the nonvanishing determinant.  Since regular maps are Zariski continuous and \(D_G\) is dense in \(U_G\),
\[
\overline{\phi_G(D_G)}^{\mathrm{Zar}}
=\overline{\phi_G(U_G)}^{\mathrm{Zar}}
=\mathcal V_G^\Sigma.
\tag{14}
\]
For clarity, the first equality follows directly from continuity: if \(x\in U_G\) and a closed set contains \(\phi_G(D_G)\), its inverse image is closed and contains the dense set \(D_G\), so it contains \(x\) and hence \(\phi_G(x)\).

The closure in (14) is irreducible.  Indeed, if it were the union of two closed sets \(C_1\cup C_2\), then
\[
U_G=\phi_G^{-1}(C_1)\cup\phi_G^{-1}(C_2).
\]
Irreducibility of \(U_G\) would put all of \(U_G\) in one inverse image, say \(\phi_G^{-1}(C_1)\); taking closures in (14) would then give \(\mathcal V_G^\Sigma\subseteq C_1\).  Thus one member already equals the whole closure.  This proves that every \(\mathcal V_G^\Sigma\) is a nonempty irreducible affine algebraic set.

For the fixed true graph \(G_0\), define
\[
\mathcal E_{G_0}:=
\bigcup_{\substack{H\in\mathcal F:\
\operatorname{SCC}(H)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0),\\
\dim\mathcal V_H^\Sigma\le\dim\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma}}
\left(\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\cap\mathcal V_H^\Sigma\right).
\tag{15}
\]
Every intersection in (15) is a proper closed subset of \(\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\).  Otherwise \(\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal V_H^\Sigma\).  Equality is excluded by (11).  Strict inclusion of irreducible affine algebraic sets forces strict increase of dimension directly from the definition of Krull dimension: append \(\mathcal V_H^\Sigma\) to any chain of irreducible closed subsets ending in \(\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\).  It would follow that
\[
\dim\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma<\dim\mathcal V_H^\Sigma,
\]
contrary to the index restriction in (15).  Since \(\mathcal F\) is finite, (15) is a finite union.  A finite union of proper closed subsets of an irreducible space is proper: repeated application of the defining two-set irreducibility property proves this by induction.  Hence
\[
\mathcal E_{G_0}\subsetneq\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma.
\tag{16}
\]

Finally take \(\Sigma\in\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma\setminus\mathcal E_{G_0}\).  The graph \(G_0\) is feasible in the minimization defining \(G^*(\Sigma)\), so
\[
\dim\mathcal V_{G^*(\Sigma)}^\Sigma
\le \dim\mathcal V_{G_0}^\Sigma.
\tag{17}
\]
If \(\operatorname{SCC}(G^*(\Sigma))\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\), feasibility of \(G^*(\Sigma)\), together with (17), would put \(\Sigma\) in one of the intersections in (15), contradicting the choice of \(\Sigma\).  Therefore
\[
\mathcal R(\Sigma)
=\operatorname{SCC}(G^*(\Sigma))
=\operatorname{SCC}(G_0).
\]
The fixed order \(\preceq\) only makes \(G^*(\Sigma)\) single valued; the argument proves that every minimum-dimensional compatible minimizer has the correct SCC partition outside (15).

statements.statement: Under the finite-candidate, compact-parameter, covariance-eigenvalue, cross-SCC separation, and iid Gaussian sampling conditions, \[\sup_{G_0\in\mathcal F,\,\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\operatorname{SCC}(\widehat G_n)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\}\le\min\left\{1,\frac{4p(p+1)\overline M^2}{n\delta^2}\right\}.\] In particular, \(\widehat G_n\) is uniformly SCC-consistent for fixed \(p\), fixed finite \(\mathcal F\), and fixed \(\delta>0\) and \(\overline M<\infty\).
statements.justification: The displayed probability bound uses the cross-SCC covariance-image separation, the upper covariance-eigenvalue bound, and iid Gaussian covariance concentration; stability, edge strength, and error scale do not enter it.
statements.gap: Chen, Drton, and Wang provide covariance-perturbation recovery for DAG source ordering; cyclic SCC model images and their explicit cross-partition margin are not treated.
statements.consumer: It gives an attaining selector for prospectively specified fixed-dimensional signaling-network families.
statements.proof_tex:
For a symmetric matrix \(A\) and \(G\in\mathcal F\), put, only within this proof,
\[
\rho_G(A):=\operatorname{dist}_F(A,\mathcal M_G)
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal M_G}\|A-B\|_F.
\]
The finite-candidate assumption makes the minimization over \(G\in\mathcal F\) finite and nonempty.  Moreover, the compact-parameter assumption includes nonemptiness of every \(\Theta_G\), so the model-image definition makes every \(\mathcal M_G\) nonempty.  Thus all the displayed distances are finite, and the minimum-distance selector is well defined after applying the fixed total-order tie breaker.

Fix \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), and abbreviate \(H=\widehat G_n\).  On the event
\[
\operatorname{SCC}(H)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0),
\]
the cross-SCC separation assumption, specialized to the fixed point \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), gives
\[
\delta
\le \inf_{B\in\mathcal M_H}\|\Sigma_0-B\|_F.
\]
For every \(B\in\mathcal M_H\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
\|\Sigma_0-B\|_F
\le \|\Sigma_0-S_n\|_F+\|S_n-B\|_F.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(B\in\mathcal M_H\), using the defining minimizing property of \(\widehat G_n\), and then using \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), yields, successively,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta
&\le \|\Sigma_0-S_n\|_F+\rho_H(S_n)\\
&\le \|\Sigma_0-S_n\|_F+\rho_{G_0}(S_n)\\
&\le 2\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\bigl\{\operatorname{SCC}(\widehat G_n)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\bigr\}
\subseteq
\bigl\{\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F\ge\delta/2\bigr\}.
\tag{1}
\]

It remains to bound the probability on the right uniformly.  Write \(\sigma_{ab}=(\Sigma_0)_{ab}\).  Under the iid centered Gaussian sampling assumption,
\[
\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}(S_n)_{ab}=\sigma_{ab},\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}\bigl((S_n)_{ab}\bigr)
=\frac1n\operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}(X_{1a}X_{1b}).
\tag{2}
\]
For completeness, the bivariate Gaussian moment-generating function is
\[
\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\exp(sX_{1a}+tX_{1b})
=\exp\!\left\{\frac12\bigl(\sigma_{aa}s^2+2\sigma_{ab}st+\sigma_{bb}t^2\bigr)\right\}.
\]
Differentiating twice in \(s\) and twice in \(t\) at \((s,t)=(0,0)\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}(X_{1a}^2X_{1b}^2)
=\sigma_{aa}\sigma_{bb}+2\sigma_{ab}^2.
\]
Since \(\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}(X_{1a}X_{1b})=\sigma_{ab}\), equation (2) therefore becomes
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}\bigl((S_n)_{ab}\bigr)
=\frac1n\bigl(\sigma_{aa}\sigma_{bb}+\sigma_{ab}^2\bigr).
\tag{3}
\]
Summing (3) over all ordered pairs \((a,b)\in V^2\) proves the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
&=\sum_{a,b\in V}\operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}\bigl((S_n)_{ab}\bigr)\\
&=\frac1n\left\{\left(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0\right)^2+\|\Sigma_0\|_F^2\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
The covariance-eigenvalue assumption gives \(\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_0)\le\overline M\).  Because \(\Sigma_0\) is positive definite and has \(p\) eigenvalues, it follows that
\[
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0\le p\overline M,\qquad
\|\Sigma_0\|_F^2=\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j(\Sigma_0)^2\le p\overline M^2.
\]
Substitution in (4) yields
\[
\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
\le \frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2}{n}.
\tag{5}
\]
The elementary pointwise inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2\ge\delta^2/4\right\}
\le \frac{4}{\delta^2}\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
\]
is valid because \(\delta>0\).  Taking expectations, and then applying (1) and (5), gives
\[
\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\!\left\{\operatorname{SCC}(\widehat G_n)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\right\}
\le \frac{4p(p+1)\overline M^2}{n\delta^2}.
\]
This probability is also at most \(1\).  The bound is independent of the chosen \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\); taking the displayed supremum proves
\[
\sup_{G_0\in\mathcal F,\,\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}}
\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\!\left\{\operatorname{SCC}(\widehat G_n)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\right\}
\le
\min\!\left\{1,\frac{4p(p+1)\overline M^2}{n\delta^2}\right\}.
\]
For fixed \(p\), \(\mathcal F\), \(\delta>0\), and \(\overline M<\infty\), the second term tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\), which is precisely the asserted uniform SCC consistency.

statements.statement: For independent sample splits of sizes \(n_1,n_2\), \[\inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\ge1-\alpha_1,\qquad \inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\in\{\operatorname{SCC}(G):G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\}\ge1-\alpha_1.\] For every true \((\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in\Theta_{G_0}\) and every \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\ne v\), \(\Pr\{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}\ge1-\alpha_2\) and \(\Pr\{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The set-valued construction keeps structural and parameter uncertainty visible instead of conditioning on one learned graph.
statements.gap: Wang, Kolar, and Drton and Strieder et al. give DAG uncertainty procedures; SCC recovery alone does not identify coefficients, so this result unions over graphs and parameter roots.
statements.consumer: A signaling analyst can report a feedback-module confidence set and a conservative equilibrium-intervention effect set without treating the selected graph as known.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For either split, let \(q\in\mathbb N\), let \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and write
\[
 S_q=\frac1q\sum_{r=1}^q X_rX_r^\top,
 \qquad X_1,\ldots,X_q\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_0).
\]
We first derive a covariance concentration inequality uniformly over the stated model family.  For indices \(a,b,c,d\in V\), the Gaussian moment-generating function is
\[
 M(t)=\mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\!\left[\exp(t^\top X_1)\right]
     =\exp\!\left(\frac12t^\top\Sigma_0t\right).
\]
Differentiating this identity four times and evaluating at \(t=0\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}[X_{1a}X_{1b}X_{1c}X_{1d}]
 =\Sigma_{0,ab}\Sigma_{0,cd}
  +\Sigma_{0,ac}\Sigma_{0,bd}
  +\Sigma_{0,ad}\Sigma_{0,bc}.
\]
Taking \(c=a\) and \(d=b\), and subtracting
\(\mathbb E[X_{1a}X_{1b}]^2=\Sigma_{0,ab}^2\), yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}(X_{1a}X_{1b})
 =\Sigma_{0,aa}\Sigma_{0,bb}+\Sigma_{0,ab}^{,2}.
\]
Independence across observations and entrywise unbiasedness of \(S_q\) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
 &=\sum_{a,b\in V}\operatorname{Var}_{\Sigma_0}((S_q)_{ab})\\
 &=\frac1q\sum_{a,b\in V}
   \left(\Sigma_{0,aa}\Sigma_{0,bb}+\Sigma_{0,ab}^{,2}\right)\\
 &=\frac{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0)^2+\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^2)}q.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
By the covariance-eigenvalue-margin assumption, every eigenvalue of the positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma_0\) is at most \(\overline M\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0\le p\overline M,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^2)\le p\overline M^2.
\]
Substitution into \((1)\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
 \le \frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2}{q}.
\tag{2}
\]
For any nonnegative random variable \(W\) and \(a>0\), the pointwise inequality
\(W\ge a\mathbf 1\{W>a\}\) implies
\(\Pr\{W>a\}\le \mathbb E[W]/a\).  Applying this fact to
\(W=\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2\), using \((2)\), and invoking the definition
\[
 r_q(\gamma)^2=\frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2}{q\gamma},
\]
we obtain
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\!\left\{\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F>r_q(\gamma)\right\}
 \le
 \frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2/q}{r_q(\gamma)^2}
 =\gamma.
\tag{3}
\]
The right-hand side of \((3)\) does not depend on \(G_0\) or \(\Sigma_0\); thus the bound is uniform over all \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\).

Apply \((3)\) to the first split with \((q,\gamma)=(n_1,\alpha_1)\), and define
\[
 \mathcal E_1
 :=\left\{\|S_{n_1}-\Sigma_0\|_F\le r_{n_1}(\alpha_1)\right\}.
\]
The iid Gaussian sampling assumption gives
\(\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1)\ge1-\alpha_1\).  Since
\(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), on \(\mathcal E_1\) the definition of distance to a set gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{dist}_F(S_{n_1},\mathcal M_{G_0})
 &=\inf_{A\in\mathcal M_{G_0}}\|S_{n_1}-A\|_F\\
 &\le \|S_{n_1}-\Sigma_0\|_F\\
 &\le r_{n_1}(\alpha_1).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the definition of \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\), this proves the event inclusion
\[
 \mathcal E_1\subseteq\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}
 \ge1-\alpha_1.
\tag{4}
\]
Whenever \(G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\), its partition \(\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\) belongs to
\(\{\operatorname{SCC}(G):G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\).  Therefore the event in \((4)\) is contained in the corresponding SCC-coverage event.  Taking the infimum of both probability bounds over \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\) proves the two asserted first-split inequalities.

We next verify that the effect-set construction is well defined under the stated stability and compactness conditions.  Fix \(G\in\mathcal F\), \((\Lambda_G,\omega)\in\Theta_G\), and distinct \(u,v\in V\).  Let \(J_u:\mathbb R^{V\setminus\{u\}}\to\mathbb R^V\) be the coordinate isometry.  Then
\[
 \Lambda_{G,-u,-u}=J_u^\top\Lambda_GJ_u,
\]
so the stability-margin assumption implies
\[
 \|\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\Lambda_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le1-\kappa<1.
\tag{5}
\]
For \(B=\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top\), the finite geometric identity and \((5)\) give
\[
 (I-B)\sum_{k=0}^N B^k=I-B^{N+1},
 \qquad
 \|B^{N+1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}le(1-\kappa)^{N+1}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Taking the operator-norm limit proves
\[
 (I-\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top)^{-1}
 =\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top)^k.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda_G)\) is finite and continuous in \(\Lambda_G\).  The same argument applied to \(\Lambda_G\) itself shows that \(I_p-\Lambda_G\) is invertible.  Because \(\omega>0\), the covariance map
\[
 (\Lambda_G,\omega)\longmapsto
 \omega(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-\top}(I_p-\Lambda_G)^{-1}
\]
is well defined, continuous, and positive definite on \(\Theta_G\).

For a realized second-split covariance \(S_{n_2}\), the set \(C_G\) is the intersection of compact \(\Theta_G\), supplied by the compact-parameter assumption, with the inverse image of a closed Frobenius ball under the continuous covariance map.  Hence \(C_G\) is compact.  Whenever \(C_G\ne\varnothing\), continuity from \((6)\) implies that the infimum and supremum defining the \(G\)-indexed interval in \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}\) are finite and attained.  These random endpoints are measurable.  Indeed, for any \(c\in\mathbb R\), the set of symmetric matrices \(S\) for which there exists \((\Lambda,\omega')\in\Theta_G\) satisfying
\[
 \|S-\Sigma_G(\Lambda,\omega')\|_F\le r_{n_2}(\alpha_2)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda)\le c
\]
is closed: from any convergent sequence of such \(S\)'s, compactness of \(\Theta_G\) supplies a convergent subsequence of witnesses, and continuity preserves both displayed inequalities in the limit.  The same argument applies with \(\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda)\ge c\).  Since \(\mathcal F\) is finite, the unions involved in \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}\) are Borel measurable.

Now fix a true parameter \(\theta_0=(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in\Theta_{G_0}\).  By the meaning of truth in the homoscedastic covariance model, and by the covariance-map and model-image definitions,
\[
 \Sigma_0
 =\Sigma_{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)
 =\omega(I_p-\Lambda_{G_0})^{-\top}(I_p-\Lambda_{G_0})^{-1}
 \in\mathcal M_{G_0}.
\tag{7}
\]
Apply \((3)\) to the second split with \((q,\gamma)=(n_2,\alpha_2)\), and let
\[
 \mathcal E_2
 :=\left\{\|S_{n_2}-\Sigma_0\|_F\le r_{n_2}(\alpha_2)\right\}.
\]
The iid Gaussian sampling assumption gives
\(\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_2)\ge1-\alpha_2\).  Equation \((7)\) and the definition of \(C_{G_0}\) imply
\[
 \mathcal E_2
 \subseteq
 \{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}
 \ge1-\alpha_2.
\tag{8}
\]

On \(\mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2\), relation \((4)\) gives
\(G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\), while \((7)\) and the definition of \(\mathcal E_2\) give
\((\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\), so in particular \(C_{G_0}\ne\varnothing\).  Therefore
\[
 \inf_{(\Lambda,\omega')\in C_{G_0}}
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda)
 \le
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})
 \le
 \sup_{(\Lambda,\omega')\in C_{G_0}}
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda).
\tag{9}
\]
The interval in \((9)\) is one of the intervals in the union defining \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2
 \subseteq
 \{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Finally, the union bound, the two instances of \((3)\), and the split-level assumption yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}
 &\ge \Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2)\\
 &\ge1-\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1^c)-\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_2^c)\\
 &\ge1-\alpha_1-\alpha_2\\
 &\ge1-\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
Independence of the splits ensures the asserted iid Gaussian law separately on each split; the final union-bound step itself needs only the two marginal probability bounds.  Together with \((4)\) and \((8)\), this proves every claim.

statements.statement: Using the changed-tail dependency-cycle handle, determine whether every dependency cycle generated by two-sided local perfect matchings is contained in a common SCC of \(K\) and \(O\), so that contraction proves Theorem 3. If this containment fails, characterize a minimal obstruction and derive a different polynomial-time comparator-pair precision-rank separator that still distinguishes every SCC-discordant pair.
statements.justification: This exposes the genuinely open multiple-tail step instead of concealing it inside the headline theorem.
statements.gap: Neither the topological proof of the acyclic case nor half-trek no-sided-intersection theory controls circular use of changed tails by replacement paths.
statements.consumer: A positive answer proves H-star; a negative answer yields the precise obstruction around which a universal alternative algebraic separator must be designed.

obligation.what_is_open: It is not determined whether every mixed changed-tail dependency cycle lies in a common strongly connected component, nor has a universal alternative comparator-pair precision separator been constructed.
obligation.obstruction: The initial edge of a supporting reversed path may be changed and have a tail connected to the original tail only by the comparator edge. This prevents assigning every dependency arc to one graph's reachability preorder and blocks the proposed contraction argument.
obligation.attempted: The common-edge substitution, single-tail contraction, maximum-outdegree-one chase, and condensation-potential routes were carried through to their exact stopping points. None controls a cycle containing initial dependencies from more than one changed tail.
obligation.partial_result: Dependency cycles whose supporting paths use only edges common to \(K\) and \(O\) admit direct path substitution and preserve the entire reachability relation.  More generally, all noninitial changed-edge dependencies on a supporting reversed \(K\)-path have tails in \(\operatorname{ch}_K(i)\), while the initial dependency may have the comparator-only child \(b\) as its tail.  The one-tail and maximum-outdegree-one propositions close the corresponding special regimes, but no proof presently forces a mixed cycle containing such initial dependencies into a common strongly connected component, and no universal alternative precision separator has been derived.

statements.statement: If \(K,O\in\mathfrak G_p\) and \(d_K(i)\ne d_O(i)\) for some \(i\in V\), then the precision Jacobians \(J_K\) and \(J_O\) represent different Jacobian matroids.
